conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand you had sudden pain in your transplanted kidney earlier today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it started in my lower right side and spread across my belly and up into my chest. I was sweating and it didn’t go away for almost an hour.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. That sounds very uncomfortable. The good news is the pain went away before you got here?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it suddenly stopped on the way in the ambulance. I feel okay now, just worried.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s reassuring. We’re going to run some tests, including an ultrasound of your transplanted kidney, to see if there’s any blockage or other issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’ve been tracking my urine output. It’s less than before, but total is around 1100 mL a day between the tube and voiding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s helpful. We’ll monitor that closely. Any fever, nausea, or chills?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, none of that. But I’ve had loose greenish stools since starting linezolid for the VRE infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a known side effect. We’ll keep an eye on it. Let’s get the ultrasound done and go from there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The ultrasound is back. There’s still hydronephrosis in the transplanted kidney. The nephrostomy tube is in a calyx but not clearly in the renal pelvis, so it might not be draining well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So the tube isn’t working right? Could that be why I had pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. The blockage may have caused pressure to build up. We’re scheduling a nephrostogram tomorrow to check the tube and possibly place a stent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A stent? What does that do?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s a small tube that goes from the kidney to the bladder, bypassing the blockage. It should help drain urine properly and prevent future pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. Will I be awake for it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll get light sedation, so you’ll be relaxed but not fully asleep. The radiologist will guide everything with imaging.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re about to start the nephrostogram. The team will check the current tube and place a stent if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready. Just let me know what’s happening.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news — the procedure went well. We confirmed the nephrostomy tube had pulled back, and there was a blockage in the upper ureter. We placed an 8 Fr x 10 cm stent across it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So the blockage is fixed? Does that mean I’m better?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The stent should relieve the obstruction. Your creatinine was 2.9 on admission — we’ll watch it closely to see if it improves.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your creatinine is down to 2.6 today — that’s a good sign the kidney is draining better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. But I’ve been feeling some jaw and shoulder pain, and burning in my chest, especially when I lie down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your cardiac enzymes four times — all negative. EKG shows your usual atrial fibrillation, but no signs of heart attack.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not my heart?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Unlikely. The pain improving when you sit up suggests reflux. We’ve consulted GI. They recommend continuing omeprazole and nystatin for thrush.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been on omeprazole before. Should I take more?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re increasing it to 40 mg twice daily. We may do an endoscopy later to check for esophagitis, but your symptoms are improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your creatinine is now 2.5. Still not where we want it, so we’re planning a kidney biopsy tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Another procedure? Is something wrong?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s to check if there’s rejection or other damage. Since your creatinine isn’t dropping fast, we want to be sure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I trust you. Do I need to stop any meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re already off Coumadin, which helps. The biopsy is low risk, and we’ll do it with ultrasound guidance.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The biopsy is done. No signs of rejection, which is excellent. But we did see donor disease, which means the kidney had some pre-existing changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not rejection, but the kidney wasn’t perfect to start with?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. That explains why recovery is slower. The stent should help, and we’ll keep supporting kidney function.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We tried capping your nephrostomy tube yesterday, but you had low urine output and a burning sensation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, only 50 cc when I tried to void. Then 120 cc came out when you uncapped the tube.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We think you were dehydrated — you were NPO for the possible endoscopy. We gave fluids, and your output improved.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I need to stay hydrated?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Very important. We’ll keep the tube open for now and reassess as an outpatient.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. What about my Coumadin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We restarted it yesterday. Your INR will be checked soon, and your PCP will manage it going forward.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs are stable. Creatinine is 2.4 — best we’ve seen. We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What do I need to do at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep the nephrostomy tube open to gravity drainage and record output daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if something seems wrong?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call the transplant office if you have fever, chills, pain, redness, or decreased output. Also, keep taking linezolid for the full 10 days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. What about the green stools?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Should improve after you finish the antibiotic. Stay hydrated and eat small, frequent meals.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my heartburn?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Continue omeprazole twice daily and nystatin for thrush. Follow up with GI in two weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Any other tests before I go?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked G6PD today because of your allergy to Bactrim. It’ll help us choose the right infection prevention med.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I remember — I had palpitations with pentamidine before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Right, so we’re being careful. We’ll decide on dapsone or another option based on the result.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set for discharge. Your condition is stable, and you’re feeling well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ll follow all the instructions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing — get your labs drawn as scheduled and follow up with your transplant team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I’m just glad the pain’s gone and the kidney is working better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re glad too. Take care, and don’t hesitate to call if anything comes up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You're welcome. Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. See you at the follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll see you then. Rest well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I plan to. Thank you for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You're doing great. Just keep up with the care plan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I’ve learned a lot this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s the best outcome — staying informed and healthy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel ready to go home now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re ready to send you off. Take it easy and call if you need anything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You're very welcome. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. See you soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll be here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. I feel safe knowing that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s what we’re here for. Have a good day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: You too, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take it easy at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. No rushing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. That’s the best medicine right now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I agree. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You're welcome. We’ll see you soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Looking forward to it. Bye for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Goodbye. Take care.
